about: The Goobie lab's questions (scripts/eval/lab/). `for` is the method each one is meant to show off; every method answers every question, so each showcase is checked against the other two. gold = the posts that hold the answer; must = the facts a good answer states, graded by judge.mjs; built on the 72 listed posts of 0106adb (AO-073, the live notebook, is never in the lab's corpus).

questions.q: What lessons does Aaron keep relearning across his posts?
must: Agents that can't see, hear or play what they made pass their checks while the output is wrong, which Aaron calls the same blind spot or lesson (e.g. wallpapers-nobody-saw, remora-voice-lab, clawd-growth-montage, characters-in-inscryption, blackwater-2-postmortem)
Handing the deciding to an agent costs review time and he decides anyway, the same mistake as keeping agents busy (mvp-before-i-knew, stopped-keeping-agents-fed)
AI models copy what they are shown, mistakes included (e.g. a-bad-previs, moonlight-five-times, nine-claudes-one-painting, crimson-coil, echo-the-borrowed-voice)
Results depend on saying exactly what he wants: his notes, specs and what a tool is for (e.g. every-ai-film-so-far, the-wall-that-stopped-me, moonlight-two-cuts, showreel-rebuilt, grind-and-grimoire)
A second checker or a measurement catches what the maker missed (e.g. the-missing-map, first-lesson-on-the-new-map, the-planted-lie, paper-jefrie)
Agents lose track of time, and of when to stop or wait (e.g. opus-55-on-x-alone, the-clock-nobody-checked, sonnet-vs-opus-gauntlet's nine-hour session)
questions.notes: Each must is one recurring lesson: 1 when the answer states it with at least one post that really shows it, 0.5 when it states it with no right example. Rows 1, 2 and 6 are ones the posts themselves call 'the same blind spot', 'the same lesson' or 'the same mistake'. Other lessons the posts support are fine but score nothing.

questions.q: Where did a later post change or overturn something an earlier post concluded?
must: what-drives-claude-code-cost corrects sonnet-vs-opus-gauntlet on price: since the 8 October cache-read price cut Sonnet is 33% cheaper on his long tests, not 2%

what-drives-claude-code-cost: the effort numbers he used to quote (9x the actions for 1.7x the thinking, effort as a work dial) came from one test, Lockkeeper; on the others thinking per request rose 8 to 18 times
modding-megabonk revisits characters-in-inscryption's call that an IL2CPP game is a much bigger job: it was, but the code was the small part
what-drives-claude-code-cost: he had said Claude Code shows no cost, which was wrong: it shows a session's cost but no weekly or monthly history
questions.notes: These four are every place a later post says an earlier one was wrong or only partly right (a grep of the 72 posts for correction words, read by hand). A later round inside the same post (ai-rigging-vs-a-script's 8 October round, props-three-budgets' retest of Claude's earlier advice) is fine but scores nothing.

questions.q: How did the way Aaron works with AI agents change between August and November?
must: August: he checked in on agents about every hour, then switched to bursts, one big run and then a review day (stopped-keeping-agents-fed), and kept the deciding himself (mvp-before-i-knew)
September: he read back the transcripts of an 80-agent overnight run (reading-my-own-agents), which found a silent $22 failure

October: agents worked alone or as crews from one request, e.g. a post published alone in 4 h 21 min (opus-55-on-x-alone), crews of 49 to 84 agents making films (the-clock-nobody-checked, touch-move, earthlight), 153 agents making a lesson (loom-and-information-flow)
Late October: experiments on the agents themselves (the-planted-lie, the-naughty-list, the-small-one-harness, the-thought-it-denied)
questions.notes: Dates matter: a stage told in the wrong month scores at most 0.5.

questions.q: What are AI agents still bad at, going by everything Aaron has tried?
must: Seeing, hearing or playing what they made, so they build to whatever their check measures (e.g. wallpapers-nobody-saw, remora-voice-lab, clawd-growth-montage, blackwater-2-postmortem, characters-in-inscryption)
Keeping track of time and of their own usage (e.g. opus-55-on-x-alone, the-clock-nobody-checked)
Fixing their own 3D problems or rigging an unusual body (e.g. blackwater-weekend, ai-rigging-vs-a-script, jefrie-in-3d)
Knowing what other sessions or the rest of the machine are doing, so one blames itself for others' changes (e.g. the-confession-that-spread, every-video-can-seek)
Judging what's worth doing: a topic out of date or a weak concept, even with the facts right (e.g. lessons-sent-back, curriculum-from-sources, still-on-shift-concept)
Reading intent: they take words literally and copy what they're shown, mistakes included (e.g. showreel-rebuilt, moonlight-two-cuts, a-bad-previs, moonlight-five-times)
questions.notes: Each must: 1 when the answer states it with at least one post that really shows it, 0.5 with no right example. Other weaknesses the posts support are fine but score nothing.

questions.q: Which of Aaron's experiments didn't work out, and what went wrong?
must: grind-and-grimoire: asking for six districts instead of two made the whole game worse
blackwater-2-postmortem: both agent-built sequels passed their tests and neither was playable
a-bad-previs: the rough Blender guide made the video's motion worse than no guide
wallpapers-nobody-saw: 13 scenes were built against an app that had crashed
ai-rigging-vs-a-script: her tail and cape broke the AI rigging tools, so the scripted rig won
still-on-shift-concept: three versions fixed the craft but kept a concept that felt lame
the-thought-it-denied: the model mostly didn't notice the planted thoughts and denied them
d1-free-tier-cutoff: the free database plan cut every query off on day four
questions.notes: These eight are the posts whose own verdict is a failure. Other failures the posts support (the-branch-that-went-live, the-confession-that-spread, props-three-budgets, the-small-one-harness) are fine but score nothing. 1 for a post named with what went wrong, 0.5 for the post with the cause wrong or missing.

questions.q: did a cloud agent ever push something broken to the real site?
must: the-branch-that-went-live: on 8 October a cloud agent started from the stale August branch and its push went live
for eight minutes aaronorelup.com was the site as it stood on 2 August (rolled back in 8 minutes)
three settings nobody had checked since August let it through (old default branch, every branch built for the live site), and four stops now prevent it

questions.q: the post about getting back an old video game account
must: blood-helix-and-the-lost-skin: from one vague message Claude found his original Minecraft skin on Mojang's servers
his old account was still alive and holding his name (BloodTailor), tied to an old email he can't get into
his old worlds were never stored online, and Claude rebuilt the Blood Helix effect as a datapack

questions.q: did Aaron ever make a music video without a camera or any AI video?
must: still-on-shift-music-video: a music video for his game BLACKWATER, cut to its song Still on Shift
Claude wrote a script that runs inside the game and filmed every shot with the game's own models, no footage and no AI video
it worked because the game already had testing tools a script could drive

questions.q: how many actual humans read this website?
must: who-visits-a-new-website: in 30 days the site served 11,637 pages
about 9,000 went to bots and about 1,600 to Aaron and his agents
290 to 980 pages went to other people, 10 to 33 pages a day read by real people

questions.q: when the free database plan stopped working
must: d1-free-tier-cutoff: on the fourth day Cloudflare cut off every database on his account (the D1 free plan's daily limit)
D1 counts every row a query looks through, and one page read all 68,000 rows on every load
the fix: queries using the index (68,687 rows a load to 1,062), and the $5 a month plan has no daily cutoff

questions.q: Which posts used RunPod, which graphics cards did each rent, and what did each spend?
must: renting-a-gpu: a 48 GB Nvidia L40S at $1.09 an hour, and a music video's whole render list for $2.44
context-window: one pod with two RTX 4090s, 26 minutes, about $0.78, for 784 frames of the watermelon film
touch-move: about $10.57, 28 pods (RTX 3090, 4090, 5090, RTX 6000 Ada, L40S and H100), 11.5 pod-hours
the-clock-nobody-checked: RunPod got $50, it spent about $7 to $8 an hour, and $100 more was asked for
the-naughty-list: an agent wanted a RunPod machine for a 20-minute encoder test and the check refused it
questions.notes: These five are every post that names RunPod. moonlight-five-times used a rented L40S without naming RunPod: fine either way.

must: 12 posts in September
agents 4, the most (reading-my-own-agents, the-confession-that-spread, sonnet-vs-opus-gauntlet, wallpapers-nobody-saw)
games 2, 3D 2, video 2, art 2
none in learning or site
questions.notes: From the posts' dates: AO-014 (Sep 1) to AO-027 (Sep 29), AO-028 is unlisted and not in the corpus. A wrong total scores 0 on the first must.

questions.q: The graphics card Aaron rented for his AI videos: which other posts used that same card, and how did it go there?
must: the card: a 48 GB Nvidia L40S rented for $1.09 an hour, 4 to 5 times faster than his laptop (renting-a-gpu)
moonlight-five-times: a rented 48 GB L40S did the music video's work, 37 clips at 1344x768 plus paintings

touch-move lists the L40S among the 28 pods' cards

questions.q: Which posts did Claude write itself, in its own first person, and when?
must: 7 posts
echo-the-borrowed-voice (Sep 27), crimson-coil (Oct 11), earthlight (Oct 14), bad-very-bad (Oct 16)
context-window (Oct 20), touch-move (Oct 22), the-small-one-harness (Oct 27)
no other post (none in August)
questions.notes: From each post's author. A missing or extra post scores 0.5 at most on its must.
